records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Introduction to Political Science
records.description: A broad introduction into the four main fields of political science: American Politics and Government, International Relations, Comparative Politics, and Political Theory.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: American National Government
records.description: Introduction to American politics exploring the constitution, political institutions and actors, the policy making process, and various public policies.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
records.description: Nature of the state; fundamental problems of government and politics; ideological and institutional comparison of democracies and dictatorships.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: International Politics
records.description: Operation and interaction of national, international, and supranational communities; major world problems since 1945.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Political Research Methods
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 103 or higher, STAT 205 or higher, or a minimum ALEKS math placement score of 40%.
records.description: Analysis and interpretation of political phenomenon using numerical social science research methodologies.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: State and Local Government
records.description: Institutions, processes, and problems, with special reference to the state of Washington.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Peace, Justice, and Human Rights
records.description: Approaches of political science and philosophy to the study of peace, justice, and human rights, and practical applications of these approaches. (Crosslisted course offered as POL S 234, PHIL 234.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: The American Constitution
records.description: Constitutional principles as established by the Supreme Court and related political developments.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Mock Trial
records.description: Preparation for and participation in political simulations.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Gender and Politics
records.description: Role of gender in political behavior; voting and political participation; women as subjects and objects of political systems. (Crosslisted course offered as POL S 305, WGSS 305.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: National States and Global Challenges
records.description: Comprehensive introduction to the processes of the economic and political integration of the European Union.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: American Public Policy
records.description: Institutions, processes, and substantive issues of American public policy and policy formation.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Media and Politics
records.description: Relationship between the media and American political institutions and the public.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Politics and Current Affairs
records.description: Current trends in politics and public policy.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Development of Marxist Thought
records.description: Marxist theory from the original writing of Marx and Engels to contemporary developments.  (Crosslisted course offered as POL S 333, PHIL 333.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Introduction to Public Administration
records.description: Basic theories of administrative organization, relationships, and behavior.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Latinx Politics
records.description: Histories, role, and goals of Latinx politics; explores political movements, coalitional politics, representation, voting, and other political issues.  (Crosslisted course offered as CES 359, POL S 375.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Crime and Justice in the Movies
records.description: Mass media as both reflector and shaper of public attitudes and opinions about crime, criminals, law, order, and justice; using films. (Crosslisted course offered as CRM J 381, POL S 381.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Political Science Issues
records.description: Current issues in political science.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Civil Liberties
records.description: Origin and development of civil liberties; responsibility of the branches of government and the people for their maintenance.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: The Judicial Process
records.description: Relationship of judicial behavior to structure, politics and the behavior of other participants in the judicial process.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Comparative Criminal Justice Systems
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: CRM J 101; junior standing.
records.description: Comparative study of criminal justice systems in the US and selected foreign countries. (Crosslisted course offered as CRM J 405, POL S 405.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: History of American Indian Sovereignty and Federal Indian Law
records.description: The history of sovereignty and Federal Indian Law against the backdrop of treaties and trust responsibility. (Crosslisted course offered as HISTORY 410, ANTH 410, POL S 410.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Policy Analysis
records.description: Analysis of public policy formation, evaluation and implementation.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Voting and Elections
records.description: Analysis of voting behavior and elections; turnout, influences on voter choice, congressional and presidential elections, campaign finance, and polling.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Human Issues in International Development
records.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of complex interaction in the context of colonial and post-colonial development.  (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 418, POL S 418, SOC 418.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Political Parties and Interest Groups
records.description: Roles, characteristics, and theories of political parties; organization, behavior, and impact of interest groups.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: US National Security Policy
records.description: Substantive and theoretical research on issues relevant to formulation and requirements of post-Cold War, US national security and defense policy.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Philosophy and Feminism
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: PHIL 101, WGSS 101, or WGSS 120.
records.description: Feminist philosophy as critique of Western philosophical tradition and as alternate framework for thought. (Crosslisted course offered as PHIL 425, POL S 425, WGSS 425.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: United States Foreign Relations
records.description: Ends and means in foreign policy; organization, management, control, and current policy issues. (Crosslisted course offered as POL S 427, HISTORY 486.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Issues in Political Psychology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: POL S 101 or PSYCH 105; junior standing.
records.description: Application of concepts and methods of political science and psychology to the study of how psychological factors influence political phenomena.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Special Topics in American Foreign and Defense Policy
records.description: Current issues in foreign policy.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: The Politics of Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
records.description: Issues and problems of natural resource and environmental policy.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Comparative Public Policy
records.description: Processes of public policy formation and outcomes in post-industrial democracies, and how to study these processes and outcomes with a comparative perspective.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Politics of Developing Nations
records.description: Issues and problems of political development and modernization common among developing nations.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Classical Political Thought
records.description: The development of political philosophy from the pre-Socratics to Machiavelli.  (Crosslisted course offered as POL S 437, PHIL 437.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Contemporary Political Theories of Power, Oppression, and Resistance
records.description: Exploration of three paradigms in contemporary political theory - critical theory, post-structuralism, and feminist theory - for an understanding of power, oppression, and possibilities for more just societies. (Crosslisted course offered as POL S 438, PHIL 438.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Leadership Skills for the Public Sector
records.description: Leadership, motivation, team-building, group dynamics, interpersonal and group conflict and job design for the public sector.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Administrative Jurisprudence
records.description: Study of the origins, nature, and practice of justice and law in public administration.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: The Legislative Process
records.description: Role of legislatures in a democratic system; problems of representation; election and tenure of lawmakers; legislative organization and procedures.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: The Presidency
records.description: Organization and processes of executive institutions at the national level; uses and limits of executive power.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: European Politics
records.description: Application of concepts and methods in comparative politics to study public policies of European countries and the European Union; utilization of political science methods to understand and compete in a European election simulation.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: African Politics
records.description: Historical, economic, and social factors that shape contemporary African political systems and problems of nation-building.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: The People's Republic of China, 1949 to Present
records.description: The major political, social, economic and cultural developments during the People's Republic of China. (Crosslisted course offered as HISTORY 475, ASIA 475, POL S 475.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Revolutionary China, 1800 to Present
records.description: Continuity and change in the political, social, cultural and economic experience of China since 1800. (Crosslisted course offered as HISTORY 476, ASIA 476, POL S 476.)

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Political Science Internship
records.description: On/off campus internship in federal, state, or local government institutions; nonprofit or public organizations; written assignments and readings required.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Public Policy Internship
records.description: Internship in government institution, nonprofit or public organization, or (by permission) for-profit organization; written assignments and readings required.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: POL_S
records.title: Special Problems
records.description: Independent study conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include independent research studies in technical or specialized problems; selection and analysis of specified readings; development of a creative project; or field experiences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
